quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Klygefa (gefurulimab) recommended for approval in the EU by (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP issued a positive opinion recommending EU approval of Alexion's Klygefa (gefurulimab) as an add-on to standard therapy for adults with anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive generalised myasthenia gravis (gMG), with once-weekly subcutaneous self-administration via autoinjector. The opinion is based on the PREVAIL Phase III trial (260 patients from 20 countries), which met its primary endpoint: improvement from baseline in MG-ADL total score at week 26 versus placebo (treatment difference: -1.6 [95% CI: -2.4, -0.8], p<0.0001), with a clinically meaningful improvement as early as week one sustained through week 26; the safety profile was consistent with C5 inhibitors eculizumab and ravulizumab. Klygefa is already approved in Japan and other countries; submissions based on PREVAIL are under review in the US, China and additional countries. The company estimates 82,500 people are diagnosed with gMG in the EU5, 66,000 of them AChR-positive. The company says that, if approved, Klygefa will be the first and only dual-binding nanobody C5 inhibitor for this population (company claim).
